method.label: Connection Method
method.help: Which Signal transport to use. REST = official signal-cli-rest-api. Bot = token-based bot server. signald = signald daemon JSON-RPC. Simple = no-auth community relay.

server_url.label: Server URL
server_url.help: Base URL of the Signal gateway / daemon. Example: https://signal.example.com or http://localhost:8080.

sender_number.label: Sender Number
sender_number.help: Registered Signal account number in E.164 format. The bot's outbound identity. Used by every method.

auth_username.label: Username
auth_username.help: Optional. HTTP Basic auth username for signal-cli-rest-api. Leave blank if the daemon is unauthenticated.

auth_password.label: Password
auth_password.help: Optional. HTTP Basic auth password for signal-cli-rest-api. Stored encrypted at rest.

bot_token.label: Bot Token
bot_token.help: Token-based Bot only. Bearer token for the Signal bot server. Issued when you register the bot with the platform. Stored encrypted at rest.

account_id.label: Account ID
account_id.help: signald method only. signald account identifier — either the E.164 phone string or the UUID assigned at `signaldctl account register`. The plugin uses it in the JSON-RPC account path.

page.title: Signals
page.subtitle: Route workflow, alert, and backup events to one or more Signal phone numbers via one of four connection methods: signal-cli-rest-api, token-based bot, signald JSON-RPC daemon, or a no-auth community relay. The plugin handles Test (cheap credential round-trip) and Send (real message to the recipient).
page.registerHint: Add a channel from the host's Notifications > Channels page and pick "Signal" as the channel_type.

help.rest: Uses the official signal-cli-rest-api Java daemon. Most flexible option; supports HTTP Basic auth. Recipients must be E.164 numbers.
help.bot: Uses a token-based Signal bot server (community bridge / Signal-compatible bot frameworks). Bearer token required; recipient channel is the phone number in E.164.
help.signald: Uses the native signald daemon's JSON-RPC 2.0 HTTP API. Account ID is the E.164 number or UUID from `signaldctl account register`.
help.simple: Uses a community relay with no authentication. Public test endpoints and self-hosted simple relays only; do not use with sensitive workflows.
help.server_url: Base URL of the Signal gateway / daemon. Example: https://signal.example.com or http://localhost:8080.
help.sender_number: Registered Signal account number in E.164 format. The bot's outbound identity. Used by every method.
help.recipients: Comma-separated list of recipient numbers in E.164 format. The plugin splits on commas and sends one Signal message per recipient.
help.auth_username: Optional. HTTP Basic auth username for signal-cli-rest-api. Leave blank if the daemon is unauthenticated.
help.auth_password: Optional. HTTP Basic auth password for signal-cli-rest-api. Encrypted at rest.
help.bot_token: Bearer token for the Signal bot server. Issued when you register the bot with the platform. Encrypted at rest.
help.account_id: signald account identifier. Either the E.164 phone string or the UUID assigned at `signaldctl account register`. The plugin uses it in the JSON-RPC account path.

error.noCommon: Server URL, Sender Number, and Recipients are required.
error.noRecipients: Recipients list is empty after trimming. Add at least one E.164 number.

guide.title: Setting up Signal notifications
guide.subtitle: Pick a connection method that matches the Signal gateway you've deployed. The four methods below are listed in order of how common they are in self-hosted setups.

step1.title: Pick a connection method
step1.body: Choose one of the four method tiles on the channel form. The Signal REST API option (signal-cli-rest-api) is the most common home-server choice. Token-based bot servers and the signald daemon are both viable; community relays are easy to start with but lack credentials.

step2.title: Install a Signal gateway
step2.body: Signal messages cannot be sent directly from McHarbor — you need a gateway that speaks the Signal protocol on your behalf. signal-cli-rest-api, signald, and most bot frameworks ship as Docker images; signal-cli-rest-api is bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api on Docker Hub.

step3.title: Register a Signal account
step3.body: Every method needs a registered Signal account that can send messages. With signal-cli-rest-api: signal-cli -u +1YOURNUMBER register (the gateway may prompt for an SMS or voice code). With signald: signaldctl account register +1YOURNUMBER. Bot servers typically handle registration inside the bot framework.

step4.title: Start the gateway
step4.body: signal-cli-rest-api default port is 8080; signald exposes 8080 by default. Run the gateway on a host that McHarbor can reach — same Docker network, LAN, or VPN tunnel.

step5.title: Verify reachability
step5.body: From the McHarbor host: curl http://:8080/v1/health. signal-cli-rest-api returns 204 when healthy. signald responds with a JSON-RPC 2.0 service-description on GET /v1/accounts.

step6.title: Fill in the channel form
step6.body: Open Settings > Notifications > Channels > Add, pick "Signal". The form shows the four method tiles; click the one that matches your gateway. The matching fields appear below.

step7.title: Enter Server URL and Sender
step7.body: Server URL = the base URL of your gateway (no trailing slash). Sender Number = the registered Signal account in E.164 format (e.g. +14155551234). These two are required for every method.

step8.title: Enter Recipients
step8.body: Comma-separated list of E.164 numbers that should receive alerts. McHarbor splits on commas and sends one Signal message per recipient, so a bad number doesn't drop the batch — only that one fails.

step9.title: Method: REST — auth (optional)
step9.body: If your signal-cli-rest-api runs behind HTTP Basic auth, fill in Username + Password. Otherwise leave both blank. Both are encrypted at rest.

step10.title: Method: Bot — token
step10.body: Paste the Bearer token issued by the bot platform. Encrypted at rest. Test calls go to GET /, so the bot must accept anonymous reads on the root endpoint.

step11.title: Method: signald — Account ID
step11.body: Paste the signald account identifier: either the E.164 phone string or the UUID assigned at signaldctl account register. The plugin routes sends to /v1/accounts//rpc.

step12.title: Test, save, and route events
step12.body: Click "Test" to confirm the credentials round-trip. Save the channel. From there, route workflow, alert, or backup-completion events to it the same way as any other McHarbor.
